clue.text: Pointless transforming it into refined fuel

indicators.note: into says the rearranged pair of letters goes inside the other rearranged word
refined means processed or reworked, so the letters of fuel are rearranged
transforming says the two letters of it change their order

explanation.surface: A complaint that converting something into purified fuel is a waste of effort.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagram signals work here: 'transforming' acts on the short pronoun and 'refined' on the fuel, and 'into' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pointless is useless or in vain, achieving nothing.

clue.text: Amateurish poet accepting fancy title

indicators.note: accepting means the poet's name takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: Dante Alighieri, the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

indicators.note: fancy here means elaborately reworked, so the letters of title are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poet unworthy of his laurels takes on a grand honorific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' looks like an adjective for the title but is the anagram signal; 'accepting' puts the result inside the Italian poet after his first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dabbler in an art without professional skill; the noun used attributively for amateurish.

clue.text: Barely free from bias

definitions.meaning: fair and impartial, as a judgement can be

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both 'only just' as an adverb and 'fair' as an adjective.

clue.text: Others dropping a hint

indicators.note: dropping means a letter is let fall from the word before it

parts.note: the remainder is the rest, the others left over

explanation.surface: Other people let fall a suggestion.
explanation.definitionFit: A prompt or nudge that jogs the memory is a hint of what to recall.

clue.text: Defying orders, perhaps, fellow learner's joining expedition

indicators.note: joining says the two short pieces sit alongside the trip

parts.note: L is for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate
an outing is a short trip or excursion

explanation.surface: A trainee goes on a school trip and ignores the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Flouting means openly disregarding; orders are one example of what is so treated, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Easy to carry, Punch picture editor might use one

parts.note: something light is not heavy to carry
to box is to punch, as in boxing

explanation.surface: A portable magazine whose picture editor wants an illuminated viewing panel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punch' looks like the old British humour magazine; it is the verb to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: An illuminated panel for viewing slides and transparencies, used by those selecting photographs.

clue.text: A nameless germ spreading disease

indicators.note: spreading suggests the letters fan out and reorder themselves

explanation.surface: An unidentified microbe propagating illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubella, a mild viral infection, is commonly called by this name.

clue.text: One female in France, say, confused and uncomfortable

parts.note: the feminine form of 'one' in French

indicators.note: confused says the letters of say are jumbled

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman muddled over what to say, ill at ease.
explanation.definitionFit: Uneasy means ill at ease, anxious and unsettled.

clue.text: Rescue bangers a veggie keeps under wraps

indicators.note: keeps under wraps says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A vegetarian conceals the sausages, saving them from the barbecue.
explanation.walkthrough: Bangers are British slang for sausages.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescue someone is to deliver them from danger.

clue.text: Coal's left out to light

indicators.note: out says the letter is removed from the word

parts.note: lignite is soft brown coal; the possessive is 'Coal is'

explanation.surface: Coal has been put outside on the left, ready for a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Coal's' as 'coal is': LIGNITE with L (left) out.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignite is to set alight, to kindle.

clue.text: Get back, i.e. revert, when ordered

indicators.note: when ordered says the letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Recovering something means going back, once commanded.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrieve is to recover or regain possession.

clue.text: Ways in front will be immeasurably better

parts.note: a way is a road, so ways are streets
ahead means in front

explanation.surface: Roads leading the field will be far superior.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal British idiom for far superior, much better than rivals.

clue.text: Result of multiplying shown in finished article

parts.note: something at an end is finished
in arithmetic the product is what multiplication yields

explanation.surface: A multiplication result displayed in a completed piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: The final output of a manufacturing process is the completed item.

clue.text: Becoming match fit

parts.note: to suit is to match, as colours do
able means fit or capable

explanation.surface: An athlete getting into shape for the big game.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming means appropriate or fitting, as clothes that flatter.

clue.text: Travel round Antipodean island briefly or Mediterranean island

indicators.note: round says the travel word wraps around the short island name

parts.note: to go is to travel
Oz is short for Australia, an island continent in the Antipodes

explanation.surface: Take a trip around Australia or some sunny European isle.
explanation.definitionFit: The second island of the Maltese archipelago lies in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Mate initially needs ten cycles as competitor

parts.note: oppo is British slang for a friend or partner

indicators.note: initially says take the first letter of the next word
cycles says the letters of ten rotate, the last moving to the front

explanation.surface: A partner first needs ten bike rides to become a racer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycles' moves the T of TEN to the end, giving ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An opponent is a rival, one who competes against you.

clue.text: One keeps moving, though certainly not disturbed

parts.note: no is an emphatic refusal
mad means mentally disturbed

explanation.surface: A restless person insists they are not unhinged.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanderer with no fixed home is forever on the move.

clue.text: Debauchee has nothing to be sorry about

indicators.note: about says the regret word wraps around the empty symbol

parts.note: to rue is to regret
O is the zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A libertine feels no remorse whatsoever.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake, a man given over to dissolute pleasures, is a debauchee.

clue.text: Build in sections and lay a fibre carpet

indicators.note: lay here means set out afresh, so the letters are arranged anew

explanation.surface: Instructions for flat-pack construction and fitting a synthetic rug.
explanation.definitionFit: To prefabricate is to manufacture parts in advance for assembly on site.

clue.text: Soundly beat hard nut

indicators.note: soundly says the word is to be heard rather than spelled

parts.note: to conquer is to defeat

explanation.surface: Thoroughly defeat a tough opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: A conker is a horse chestnut, used in the British children's game of conkers.
explanation.definitionFit: The horse chestnut seed is famously hard, especially when baked for the game.

clue.text: Court order that's mostly in pen

indicators.note: mostly says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to pen is to write

explanation.surface: A judicial instruction that is largely handwritten.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal written command issued by a court is a writ.

clue.text: Tense, organised bedspread to cut temperature, becoming calm

annotationWithheld.why: Tense, organised bedspread to cut temperature, becoming calm (8): parse is T (tense) + RAN (organised) + QUIL(T) (bedspread less T for temperature), but the checker reads the cut T beside the leading T as a moved letter and refuses it as an add-then-delete; no move parse is honest
annotationWithheld.clue: Tense, organised bedspread to cut temperature, becoming calm

clue.text: Partly honour Dutch in another language

indicators.note: Partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Paying partial tribute to the Netherlands in a foreign tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Urdu, the national language of Pakistan, is another language than English.

clue.text: River that makes a U-bend

indicators.note: makes says the letters are formed into something new

explanation.surface: A waterway that winds in a tight curve.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danube is a major European river flowing to the Black Sea.

clue.text: Like Olive perhaps, drunk

definitions.meaning: an olive with its pit removed is pitted, as a fruit can be
intoxicated, slang for very high or inebriated

explanation.surface: Olive was intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Olive' is capitalised to look like a woman's name; it is the fruit with its pit removed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both having had the pits removed and heavily intoxicated.

clue.text: Covered second edition about island

indicators.note: about says the edition letters go around the island

parts.note: Crete is the large Greek island

explanation.surface: A second printing reported on a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: To secrete something is to hide it, so it is concealed or covered.
